renderer: render_fig5.py (hand-written; house style imported from chart_style/chart_geometry)
title: A refit threshold buys recall and loses specificity
ylabel:
False-positive rate
(fraction of eligible undeclared checkpoints)

series.label: LORCO refit threshold tau = -1.7156
series.colour_role: red (substituted: house palette amber, see notes)

error_bars: 95% Wilson intervals, drawn asymmetrically from ci_low/ci_high
notes: The specification asked for green/red. The house style forbids a red/green series pair (it is the one pair that collapses under protanopia/deuteranopia) and the audited palette contains no red, so the second series uses the palette amber #DE8F05 against green #029E73. Semantics are carried by the legend labels.
Zero-height green bars are drawn as a hairline baseline marker so the category is visibly measured rather than missing; the plotted value remains 0.000 and only the upper Wilson bound extends.

Legend requested top-right; at 16:9 with ylim capped at 0.30 the upper-right corner is occupied by the base group's '12/78' count above its 0.250 Wilson bound, and the legibility gate refuses the overprint. The legend is therefore placed below the axes as a two-column figure legend — the same move the house style makes automatically when an in-axes legend would cover the data.
caption: False-positive rate on eligible undeclared Hub checkpoints at the panel-fitted operating point tau = -2.7415 and at the leave-one-recipe-class-out refit tau = -1.7156, split by whether the checkpoint declares a chat template. The refit shifts the threshold by 1.026 log-units, 8.04 times the 0.128-log-unit shift that already produces a first false positive, and costs specificity disproportionately on base models. Error bars are 95% Wilson intervals.
